chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When a man commits fornication with a woman, her daughter does not become permissible to him forever, even if he had previously married the daughter and had not yet consummated the marriage, then his marriage is annulled. And if he married the daughter and consummated the marriage, then later committed fornication with her mother, his fornication with the mother does not annul the marriage to the daughter, provided he had already entered into her. And this is His saying: 'That which is forbidden does not annul that which is permissible, if it is thus.'

key_terms.لَا يُفْسِدُ الْحَرَامُ الْحَلَالَ: That which is forbidden does not annul that which is permissible

ai.seo_question: Does fornication with a mother invalidate a man's marriage to her daughter?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-istibsar clarifies the fiqh of 'fujur' (fornication) as a specific cause for marital prohibition, distinguishing it from general zina by emphasizing the physical act's impact on lineage and contract validity. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that 'al-haram la yufsidu al-halal' (the forbidden does not nullify the permissible) when the conditions of the permissible act are met, a nuance critical in distinguishing between pre-consummation annulment and post-consummation stability. The ruling underscores the practical implication that a man's illicit relationship with a mother does not retroactively invalidate his lawful marriage to her daughter, provided consummation occurred.
